request: Per-allocation-site (or at least per-marker) breakdown of managed heap allocation bytes during frames 462-481, correlated with the GarbageCollector.CollectIncremental burst window identified in F3.
reason: queryFrameCounters only exposes gc_allocated_in_frame as a single whole-frame total per frame; it cannot attribute which specific marker/subsystem/script call is allocating during this 20-frame burst window. Without this, it is impossible to confirm which system is driving the periodic incremental GC pressure feeding into the frame-483 GC.Collect stall (F2/F3).
hypothesisToTest: That a specific recurring gameplay system (e.g. camera/map update, entity sync, or Lua tick) is allocating steadily during frames 462-481, causing the incremental GC to build up pressure that resolves in a full collect at frame 483.

request: Time series or event log of the LoaderManagerTryUnloadPending pending-unload queue size (number of assets queued for unload) around frames 80, 102, 146, 414, 464.
reason: None of the 8 tools expose asset/resource manager internal state (queue depth, asset counts) -- they only see marker timing (selfMs/totalMs) in the call tree. F5 established that this marker spikes to ~30ms on 5 specific frames but cannot explain why those specific frames trigger a larger unload batch than neighboring frames.
hypothesisToTest: That the pending-unload queue accumulates over some interval and periodically drains in a single expensive frame, and that queue depth at spike time correlates with the ~30ms cost observed.

request: Per-camera (not just per-frame) breakdown of batches / set_pass_calls / triangles for frames using URP.RenderSingleCamera, to determine whether the 10.64ms/frame rendering subtree cost (F7) scales primarily with draw call count, transparent overdraw, or shader complexity.

hypothesisToTest: That reducing draw call count or transparent overdraw for the main camera would proportionally reduce URP.RenderSingleCamera's subtree cost, as opposed to the cost being inherent to shader/pass complexity regardless of draw call count.
